atoms.b: Paper, card and foil can be ((cut)) with ((scissors)). You can also ((tear)) paper and card quite easily with your bare hands.

hint.text: Foil is metal which has been rolled out into a very thin sheet. Its thinness allows it to be cut and bent easily.

atoms.b: On the other hand, if you want to cut wood or metal, it is best to use a ((saw)). ((Metal)) can also be bent into shape quite easily.
You can cut glass by scoring it with a ((glass_cutter)). This means scratching a line along its surface. The glass will then ((break)) exactly along this line.

instruction.text: Who works with which material? Select the matching picture.

feedback.correct: Carpenters work with wood. Some use it to construct frames, or even entire buildings. Other carpenters specialise in making smaller items such as furniture.
With the help of machines, plastics engineers manufacture many objects, for example toys and bottles, from synthetic materials.
Glassmakers engrave glass and make molten glass into containers such as vases and bottles.
Welders use heat to fuse pieces of metal together.

instruction.text: Who works with which material? Select the matching picture.

feedback.correct: Blacksmiths work with hot iron and produce metal objects such as tools, railings and even sculptures.
Stonemasons cut and carve stone to make things such as buildings and sculptures.
Tailors create, alter and repair different types of clothing.
Bookbinders bind sheets of paper and add a cover to create a finished book.
